Jonas / Marissa — initial legal draft and clarifications below. I'll prepare a mark-up (DPA_Annex_draft_redline.docx) and put comments where we propose alternate language. Highlights: 

- DPA annex: Redwood uses the standard processor annex with three narrow deviations described in the attached redline (liability cap language tailored for hosted/dedicated offerings; audit scope limited to security operations; and an explicit carve-out for model weights retention in Private on-prem deployments). See redline comments for rationale.
- Transfers: we support SCCs and rely on the EU-US DPF when available; we also provide contractual binding transfer mechanisms plus operational controls (region pinning). For Lumen's EU-only requirement, we can offer a Private deployment (VPC in eu-west-1) and commit to region-only routing via routing policy: region_pin = eu. (Answer C-3, C-12).
- Subprocessors: will provide CSV export of active subprocessors over last 12 months plus dates of engagement. For certain cloud infra partners we list limited roles (compute / storage).

Open Qs for procurement/legal: does Lumen require the processor to accept full audit (on-site) or is a virtual SOC2 + evidence bundle sufficient? That impacts timeline for execution of the redline.

I will upload the redline to the Drive and share a DocuSign-ready copy if you want to advance contract execution.

Kimberly

Following up with the ops/engineering inputs that map to the spreadsheet IDs D-1..D-10. I'll place a consolidated evidence bundle in the Drive (Redwood_DPF-Evidence_20260805.zip) but key points here: 

- Routing & residency: runtime supports policy-based routing. Policies may be set per-customer or per-route; for EU-only workloads we can enforce region_pin = eu and we run inference in eu-west-1 or in customer-provided on-prem. For Hosted customers we default to the nearest region; Dedicated/Private customers can pin.
- Model routing & fallbacks: we implement fallback variants (smaller quantized variants) and automated routing tiers (hosted -> dedicated -> private) as part of SLA fallbacks. We log routing decisions per request with request_id, timestamp, and chosen model_variant; logs are retained per the contract retention window and can be exported via secure S3 push.
- KMS & keys: we integrate with customer KMS (BYOK) and support HSM-backed keys for key wrap; keys may be regionally scoped. At-rest encryption uses AES-256; in-transit uses TLS1.3 with mutual auth for inter-service links.
- KV cache & data residency: KV cache may be enabled per-customer; for regulated customers we recommend disabling shared prefix cache or enabling isolated caching (per-customer cache instances) to avoid co-mingling.
- Audit & evidence: we provide an evidence package: architecture diagram, routing policy sample, KMS integration guide, logging schema, and a sample per-request log record.

I can host a 45-minute technical walkthrough (Wed or Thu) to walk Lumen's engineers through the evidence artifacts.

Marissa — Operations
